summary: Release A/B final P0 corrections. Regression is green: 95/95 across iteration 336/337 suites (identity, onboarding, api_iter336, iter337), sage_sicon_customer_import, sage_sicon_import_independent, sicon_onboarding_jun2026, customer_import_release_a and the 3 AFS shared-customer suites. New suite tests/test_release_ab_iter338.py: 8 of 12 pass, 4 fail on real defects. Verified: the nightly sync does nothing unless SICON_NIGHTLY_SYNC_ENABLED=true (tested unset and 'false'). run_equipment_sync in the Pulse workspace returns 'blocked' and writes no equipment and no links. Onboarding, equipment and case syncs share one 'estate' lock document. Sage: tenant CRM owner gets 403 on all 5 endpoints. For the admin, the push returns 403 'read-only'. The pull gives 400 when no company is configured and 409 when the typed company disagrees, and accepts a case-insensitive match or company_id. With SAGE_ALLOW_WRITES=true the guard is passed (503, nothing configured, no network). Proposed sites over HTTP (/proposed-sites/{id}/{decision}): Sage postcode twin gives 409 then force confirms; link sets invoice_customer_ref; a second reject gives 409; Sicon link to a site holding another sub-location gives 409 and the proposal is released; Sicon confirm keeps sicon_sub_location_id and sicon_source with invoice_customer_ref '' and attaches equipment. Delegate history records grant, extend and revoke (3 entries, correct 'revoked'), and an empty grant removes access. Review Centre groups held equipment into one 'Held Sicon equipment (customer not imported)' row per code. UI (Playwright, minted admin token): Review Centre shows the held group row ('3 equipment record(s) for Sicon customer TSTUIHELD', high priority). Confirm on a seeded Sicon proposed site works from the UI, and the DB site keeps sub-location and source. Import Centre: ci-company-input is 'Pulse Fitness', maxlength 40. The Sicon card renders the latest preview (failed: preview Sicon is localhost, 404, expected). No page errors.

critical.issue: Cross-tenant: reserve_link and _key_for_write look up the scoped key (source_company + id) without the organisation. When customer org C2 creates a Sicon id that customer C1 already holds under the same connection, C2's 'new' record returns C1's asset id as action 'linked'. get_link correctly hides C1's link from C2 (classify says 'new'), so the create path contradicts the read path. In preview every org without its own sicon_config shares the connection 'localhost:51080#2' from the env, so this is reachable. The matching upsert_link path also flips C1's link to 'conflict' (mutates another tenant's link). Test: test_customer_org_cannot_claim_other_customers_link.

Follows from the issue above: a Sicon equipment id first applied for customer A, later re-assigned in Sicon to customer B, gets B's site written onto A's asset. apply returns A's asset id, then equipment.update_one({id}, site_id=B site) with no organisation filter. Cross-tenant write, and the record is not held for review. Test: test_onboarding_moved_equipment_no_cross_tenant_write.

minor.issue: SOURCE_CTX leaks between orgs when nightly sync is enabled. run_equipment_sync never sets SOURCE_CTX, but run_case_sync does, and the nightly loop runs every org in one task. So org B's equipment links get scoped by org A's connection (stored 'sicon-a.test#11' instead of 'sicon-b.test#22'). Inactive in preview because the flag is off. Fix: set SOURCE_CTX at the start of run_equipment_sync (and reset the token in a finally) in every run, or run each org in contextvars.copy_context(). Test: test_nightly_source_ctx_not_leaked_between_orgs.

One approved preview can be applied any number of times; there is no single-use or consumed flag. Records with a Sicon id are protected by links. A record without a Sicon id (noid: key, no serial) passes the fingerprint check every time and creates a new asset on each apply: 2 assets after 2 applies. The noid key correctly blocks changed records. Test: test_noid_records_respect_preview.
Sicon-sourced proposed sites are labelled source 'Sage address' and show an empty Account column. They should say 'Sicon sub-location'.
This route named in the brief does not exist. The real route is POST /proposed-sites/{id}/{confirm|link|reject}?link_site_id=&force=, which the frontend uses and which was tested.

Re-sync site recognition in decide_site and the link 409 check ignore sicon_source (only sicon_sub_location_id is compared). operational_site does use sicon_source. If an exception happens after the find_one_and_update, the proposal stays stuck in 'deciding'.
The finally block deletes every sicon_sync_runs doc with status 'blocked' for the operator org, not only the run the test created.

issues: A Sicon proposed site row shows 'Sage address' as its source and has no account ref, which is misleading

action_items: Scope reserve_link/_key_for_write/upsert_link writes by organisation, unless the caller is the Pulse workspace. When another customer org already holds the id under the same connection, return a conflict (hold for review), never that org's asset id, and never mutate its link status.
In _equipment_phase, filter the site_id update by organization_id=dest, and treat 'owner belongs to another org' as held or conflict.
Set links.SOURCE_CTX inside run_equipment_sync, reset it after each run, and isolate each org in the nightly loop.
Make an approved preview single-use (mark it consumed on apply, or reject a second apply), or reserve the noid: key so a no-id record cannot be created twice.
Label Sicon proposed sites as source 'Sicon sub-location' in the Review Centre.
critical_code_review_comments: customer_account_import.py is 1670 lines and sicon_import.py is 878: split them.
crm_sage200._require_pulse_admin does not accept role == PULSE_ROLE, while customer_account_import._is_full_admin does. The Pulse-admin definition is inconsistent.

The is-Pulse-org lookup is duplicated in _in_pulse_org, onboarding_projects._require_pulse_or_master, set_delegate and sicon_links.is_pulse_workspace. Extract one helper. is_pulse_workspace caches for 300 s, so a revoked operator flag lingers.

The operator-workspace onboarding lock is taken on the OP org, while a customer org's own run_equipment_sync locks on the customer org. Both write the same customer estate, so they are not mutually exclusive.
seed_data_creation: Only temporary TST data (orgs, sites, proposed sites, conflicts, sicon_config rows tagged 'tst'), each removed by id or tag; leftover check returned 0. UI seed TST-ui-org-338 was created and removed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest tests/test_release_ab_iter338.py -p no:xdist. The 4 failing tests encode the expected behaviour for the defects. Proposed-site HTTP route: /api/master-admin/customer-import/proposed-sites/{id}/{decision}. UI: put the minted token (utils.auth.create_token(admin id)) in localStorage 'token' and the ga_session cookie, then open /master-admin?section=onboarding&tab=review (Review Centre) or tab=import-centre&type=sage_accounts. In preview every org without its own sicon_config shares the connection 'localhost:51080#2' (env SICON_COMPANY_ID=2), so cross-org link collisions are reachable. The Sicon onboarding preview button was not clicked, because the preview Sicon is localhost and returns 404.
rca of the issue: The cross-tenant leak comes from sicon_links._key_for_write and reserve_link. They resolve the write key from (source_company, external id) only, while get_link applies an org guard on reads. Repro: SOURCE_CTX='shared#9'; apply_equipment_record(C1, X, new) creates A1; classify_equipment(X, C2) returns 'new'; apply_equipment_record(C2, X, new) returns {'linked', A1}. In onboarding the following site_id update by id then writes into C1's asset. Fix: add an organisation guard on writes for non-workspace callers and a dest-org filter on the site update.
